primaryContributions.contribution: Disease-pattern measurement, bias/confounding/causality, screening and health-needs assessment provide a bounded population-research complement to brain health and ageing. The Zeeland project is not guaranteed to study brain disease.

Cell structure, metabolism, DNA/heredity, gene expression and biotechnology establish the molecular and cellular foundations of brain science. Class-selected additions are not treated as guaranteed neural topics.

Direct psychological and neuroscientific explanations of mental processes: signalling, brain anatomy/development, learning, disorders and research approaches supply the integrative brain/behaviour foundation.

Python programming, recursion, object-oriented design, testing and debugging supply concrete computational tools for modelling and analysing brain/behavioural questions; projects are not guaranteed neuroscience.

Calculus, differential equations, numerical methods and dynamic-model implementation provide mathematical methods for biological and cognitive modelling, without claiming that the actual model project is neural.

Direct comparative nervous-system and brain anatomy, regulatory behaviour, rhythms/sleep, lifestyle drugs and mood/eating disorders support neural mechanisms and brain-health inquiry, with animal-research ethics.

Molecular/cellular organisation, proteins, bioenergetics, gene regulation and signalling supply mechanisms for neural-cell function; its drug-target literature work is biomedical and not guaranteed brain-specific.
Mandatory Year-1 Personal & Professional Development.

Direct neuroanatomy/neurophysiology, attention, memory, emotion and cognitive control connect neural systems to behaviour; the attentional-blink experiment and research proposal develop cognitive-neuroscience investigation.

Enzyme regulation, biomolecules and energy/lipid/nitrogen metabolism provide a concrete molecular complement to brain-cell biology. The disease project remains broadly biochemical, not a promised neurological case.
Experimental design and multivariable R-based statistical analysis support behavioural/neuroscience data questions through regression, repeated measures, model checking and scientific reporting.
Linear systems, eigenvalues, transformations, dynamical systems, least squares and principal components supply matrix methods for computational models and high-dimensional brain/behavioural data.

The official description directly supports neural sensory processing and goal-directed action using cognitive-neuroscience/neuropsychological approaches; no finer experimental or imaging methods are invented.

Biopsychosocial explanations, classification and evidence synthesis for mental disorders support the brain-function/dysfunction and treatment interest; this is psychological analysis, not clinical qualification.

Systematic review, effect sizes, bias appraisal and R-based meta-analysis support critical synthesis of brain, medical and behavioural findings; no substitute for laboratory or neural recording is claimed.

Molecular/microbial laboratory methods, microscopy, protein/DNA analysis, PCR and reproducible reporting provide experimental life-science tools. They do not reproduce a dedicated brain-recording or neurophysiology practical.

Nervous-system drug applications and a psychoactive-drug experimental-design project directly strengthen treatment/mechanism inquiry, supported by pharmacodynamics, kinetics and dose-response modelling.

Genetic variation, epigenetics, molecular diagnosis/treatment and research-grant design complement molecular mechanisms of disease relevant to brain-disorder inquiry; broad cancer/inflammation content is not called neuroscience.
Probability, estimation, hypothesis tests, Bayesian reasoning and Monte Carlo methods supply rigorous inference and uncertainty tools for experimental and computational brain science.
Statistical learning, regression/classification, validation and model choice support prediction and analysis of brain/behavioural data; they do not establish biophysical neural simulation.

Neural-network implementation, backpropagation, regularisation and predictive evaluation supply computational learning tools. Artificial network architectures are not equated to biological neurons or a dedicated computational-neurobiology course.

Cognitive, emotional and physical development from prenatal life to ageing and developmental psychopathology support lifespan questions about brain/behaviour; the adult life-story interview is not a neural measurement.
The official description supports multivariate calculus, differential equations, complex-valued functions and computer algebra for modelling foundations. Absent enrichment is not reconstructed.

Moral reasoning, theories, argument evaluation and ethical research essays provide a specific foundation for judging human/animal research and brain/AI applications; specialist neuroethics or AI-law content is not asserted.

primaryDisposition: Retain as a strengthened provisional closest-response research artifact; complete external comparability and academic approval remain blocked.

courseCorrection.reason: The current Functional Anatomy evidence concerns mainly body regions and organ systems; it does not establish the specialist neuroanatomy contribution that its position in a brain-science plan could suggest. Pharmacology explicitly teaches nervous-system drugs and a psychoactive-drug research proposal, strengthening the evidenced brain-disorder/treatment priority.
courseCorrection.scheduleChange: Epidemiology moves from term 5 to term 1, PPD moves from term 1 to term 2, and Pharmacology occupies term 5. HCBGATE101 precedes Pharmacology. All other primary courses and term assignments retained.

rejectedPrototype.label: Population and Public Health: From Brain and Behavioural Health to Health Systems and Policy
rejectedPrototype.disposition: Rejected as constructed; not an approved or accepted additional UCR alternative.
rejectedPrototype.reason: A valid general population/public-health programme is not by itself a material response to this target’s defining psychology/biology/computation of the brain. This prototype has introductory Brain & Behavior and several clinical/health courses but omits the direct Neurobiology, Higher Order Functions, Perception & Action and computational/mathematical sequence while giving substantial weight to sociology, economics, international relations and general biomedical/environmental study. Current minor names and possible healthcare careers do not repair that lost brain-science anchor.
rejectedPrototype.preserved: Its original schedule, 24 course facts and earlier feasibility verification remain in the historical source artifact; fresh mechanical validation passed, but it is no longer treated as an academically accepted provisional option.

stoppingDecision: No third alternative generated after rejecting the second prototype. The exact additional-concept and generator-coverage decision remains unfinished pending the current cohort evidence; there is no final one-programme comparison approval.
